author: Russell Brand
description:
Forty farming families. One shared tractor. A $4 million infrastructure network built on community investment instead of corporate dependency — and the people at Caterpillar and the centralized food supply chain are not happy about it. Russell Brand breaks down why the model of decentralized communal farming is not just economically smarter but spiritually antithetical to the system that profits from individual isolation, debt, and the belief that you need to own everything yourself to be whole. Big Food needs you broken and separate. This is what the alternative actually looks like.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand sits down and delivers his most unfiltered assessment yet of Donald Trump, tracing his initial appeal back to a single exchange in the 2016 primaries where Trump told Hillary Clinton to her face that she never changed the tax code because all her friends exploit it the same way he does. Russell argues that Trump was not a politician but something conjured from the collective imagination of a country that had watched Obama bail out the banks in 2008, preside over the largest foreclosure of ordinary American homes in history, and confirm once and for all that establishment politics had become nothing more than a casting exercise. Whether Trump delivered on the diagnosis is a different question entirely.
